subject: environmental
audience: FE Environmental candidates and environmental engineering students
title: The Landfill That Lasted 3.42 Years, Not 4.11
featured_title: THE LANDFILL THAT LASTED 3.42 YEARS, NOT 4.11

presentation.challenge: Ignoring daily cover made the landfill appear to last 4.11 years. Including 20% cover-volume use reduced the life to about 3.42 years.

practice.primary_question: How do waste mass, compacted density, cover-volume use, and available airspace determine landfill life?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Using compacted waste volume alone to estimate landfill life and ignoring the specified airspace consumed by cover material.

case_dna.target_misconception: Available landfill airspace should be divided only by compacted waste volume, even when cover is stated to consume additional airspace.
case_dna.why_plausible: Waste density directly converts mass to volume, so it is easy to stop before accounting for non-waste material occupying the same landfill capacity.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: At 200 ton/day and 1200 lb/yd³, compacted waste uses 333.3 yd³/day. Adding cover equal to 20% of waste volume raises total airspace use to 400 yd³/day, so 500,000 yd³ lasts 1250 days or about 3.42 years.
case_dna.corrected_model: Convert waste mass to compacted volume, add the specified cover-volume fraction, then divide available landfill airspace by total daily airspace consumption.

problem_statement: A landfill has 500,000 yd³ of available airspace. It receives 200 ton/day of solid waste compacted to 1200 lb/yd³. Daily cover and operational material consume additional volume equal to 20% of the compacted waste volume. A capacity note ignores cover and reports about 4.11 years of life. Determine the correct landfill life.
fixed_constraints: Cover volume=20% of compacted waste volume

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The waste-volume calculation was correct. The total airspace use was not.
gates.prompt: What must be added after converting waste mass to compacted volume?

options.label: Use total daily airspace=(waste mass/density)×1.20
options.reason: The specified cover occupies 20% additional airspace relative to compacted waste volume.

options.label: Use only waste mass/density
options.reason: That ignores the stated cover-volume demand.

options.label: Divide waste volume by 1.20
options.reason: Cover increases, rather than decreases, total airspace consumption.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict landfill life
gates.prompt: Enter the landfill life in years.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Track daily airspace consumption
gates.result: The landfill life is about 3.42 years.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the landfill life
gates.success: Waste volume=333.3 yd³/day, total airspace use=400 yd³/day, and life=1250 days≈3.42 years.
gates.hint: Convert tons to pounds before using the compacted density.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Cover material consumes real landfill capacity

cards.text: Total=400 yd³/day, so life=500,000/400=1250 days≈3.42 years.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the landfill-capacity note
report: C1. The landfill has 500,000 yd³ available.
C2. Compacted waste uses about 333.3 yd³/day.
C3. Therefore landfill life is about 4.11 years.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: This compacted waste-volume calculation is correct.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It ignores the additional 20% airspace consumed by cover material.

evidence_choices.label: Total airspace use=333.3×1.20=400 yd³/day
evidence_choices.reason: The cover volume must be included before calculating life.

correction.template: The landfill has about {life_years} years of life under the stated operating assumptions.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Extend the same airspace to 5 years
gates.constraint: Keep density and the 20% cover fraction unchanged.

options.label: Reduce average waste acceptance to about 137 ton/day
options.reason: 500,000 yd³ over 1825 days permits about 274 yd³/day total, corresponding to about 137 ton/day of waste.

options.label: Increase to 240 ton/day
options.reason: Higher daily mass shortens landfill life.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply the same airspace method
gates.prompt: A landfill receives 120 ton/day at 1000 lb/yd³ with cover equal to 25% of waste volume. How much total airspace is used per day?

options.label: 300 yd³/day
options.reason: Waste volume=240 yd³/day and total=240×1.25=300 yd³/day.

options.label: 192 yd³/day
options.reason: That incorrectly divides by the cover factor.

gates.explanation: Total daily airspace equals compacted waste volume plus the specified cover-volume fraction.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the landfill-life calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that landfill life must account for all specified materials consuming airspace, not only compacted waste.

items.label: What failed
items.value: The capacity calculation ignored cover-volume consumption.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: Cover and operational material occupy part of the same finite landfill airspace.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Convert mass to compacted waste volume, add cover volume, then divide total airspace by daily use.

seo.seo_title: Landfill Airspace and Life With Cover Volume | FE Environmental E-077
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Environmental Case E-077: 500,000 yd³ of airspace receiving 200 ton/day lasts about 3.42 years when 20% cover volume is included.
seo.excerpt: Landfill capacity is consumed by more than compacted waste. Cover material can materially reduce the expected operating life.
seo.direct_answer: At 200 ton/day and 1200 lb/yd³, compacted waste occupies 333.3 yd³/day. Adding 20% cover gives 400 yd³/day total airspace use. Therefore 500,000 yd³ lasts 1250 days, or about 3.42 years.

faqs.q: How do you estimate landfill life from available airspace?
faqs.a: Divide available airspace by total daily airspace consumption, including specified cover or operational material.

faqs.q: Why does cover reduce landfill life?
faqs.a: Because cover occupies part of the same finite landfill volume.
